## Summary vs gemma3:4b (CPU laptop) and recommendation

| Metric | gemma3:4b (CPU) | gemma-3-12b-it (DeepInfra) | gemma-3-27b-it (DeepInfra) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Answer TTFT median / p95 (s) | 0.39 / 1.57 (cold run 1: 1.41; CPU-only table: 23.2 cold) | 0.57 / 0.76 | 0.71 / 2.25 |
| Answer total median / p95 (s) | 8.47 / 17.40 (CPU-only: 8.17 / 32.18) | 1.57 / 2.21 | 3.03 / 7.93 |
| Citation-valid | 88% | 92% | 100% |
| In-RAG valid | 65% | 69% | 75% |
| In-RAG false refusal | 25% | 25% | 25% |
| In-RAG fallback to extractive | 10% | 6% | 0% |
| Out-of-RAG refused | 100% | 100% | 100% |
| Off-topic leaks | 0/36 | 0/36 | 0/36 |
| must_mention | 50% | 100% | 100% |

Notes: 25% in-RAG false refusal is identical across sizes, so it comes from retrieval (PT-BR recall@1 81% vs EN 100%; weak PT questions such as in-04, in-14 land on case-studies/arm-templates) and prompt strictness, not model size. Out-of-RAG refusal is 100% everywhere, and the min_score gate does not separate out-of-corpus (top-1 >= 0.5 for 92-100% of those), so refusal depends on the model.

Recommendation: use gemma-3-27b-it as primary (only size with 0% fallback and 100% citation-valid; worst-case answer total 7.9 s). gemma-3-12b-it is a cheaper, faster second choice (p95 2.2 s) with 6% fallback and 92% citation validity; the quality gap is small, so pick 12b if cost matters. Timeouts: first token 15 s and total 60 s are generous; measured p95 TTFT is 2.3 s and p95 total 7.9 s, so `LLM_FIRST_TOKEN_TIMEOUT_S=10` and `LLM_TIMEOUT_S=30` would still leave margin and fail over to extractive faster. Keeping 15/60 is safe. Largest remaining gain is PT-BR retrieval (bge prefix or multilingual embeddings), not a bigger model.
